Subject: Follow-up: fallback behavior and SLOs after demo

Hi Irene —

Thanks again for the product walkthrough earlier today. A couple items came up on our side related to failover/fallback behavior that we want clarified before the next exec review:

- How does Redwood route when a primary region becomes unhealthy? Specifically: instant redirect vs queued retry vs degrade to cheaper model variant.
- Are rate limits evaluated per-customer or per-deployment? We have bursty traffic during claims cycles and want to understand tail behavior.
- Error budget handling: if we exceed target availability for a window, what automated fallthroughs occur?

We'd like a short matrix showing behavior vs the hyperscalers (GCP/Azure) for the above items and a proposed test plan we can run together. Can you include runbook-level steps and expected telemetry so our SREs can validate?

Elena
VP Product, Medisys

> Hi Elena — great questions, and really appreciate the clarity on what your SREs will need. I've attached a concise service-fallback matrix and a short playbook with proposed test steps. High level answers below and then a suggested joint test plan.
>
> High-level behavior (Redwood):
> - Routing: smart-routing policy prefers same-region pinned pools; on region degradation we automatically re-route to the next healthy region (cross-region failover) with 1) in-flight request draining, 2) KV cache warm-start where possible, and 3) optional model-variant fallback (smaller quantized model) if latency SLO would otherwise be missed.
> - Rate limits: default limits are per-customer API key; we support per-deployment override. Throttling is token-bucket based with a short adaptive backoff that is observable in the console.
> - Error budgets & automation: depending on your policy we can 1) prioritize canary traffic, 2) engage model-variant fallthrough, or 3) route to dedicated lower-cost capacity. We expose the error budget metrics and allow automated policy triggers (canary -> fallback) in the console.
>
> Proposed joint tests (summary):
> 1) Regional failover probe (simulate AZ + region latency spike): measure failover time, per-request latency spike, and KV hit rate.
> 2) Burst rate-limit stress: send production-shaped bursts (90th/99th pct shapes) to validate tail-QPS behavior and throttling response.
> 3) Error-budget exceed scenario: artificially reduce capacity in primary pool and observe automatic fallthrough to model-variant / dedicated pool and log telemetry.
>
> I've marked expected telemetry fields in the attached playbook and included a small matrix comparing Redwood vs GCP/Azure for those behaviors. Proposed timeline: run tests with Redwood engineers Wed next week (May 5) and share raw traces within 24h.
>
> Two quick asks from our side:
> - Can your SREs be available for a 60-minute joint run?
> - Is 0.5% short-term error budget (per hour) acceptable as your acceptance criteria for the test?
>
> I'll loop Ben and Marcus to add test-run specifics and any constraints.
>
> Thanks —
> Irene Choi
> Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
> On behalf of the POC team
> Attachment: service-fallback-matrix.pdf (PDF, 92KB); test-run-playbook.md (text)

> Team — adding a few technical constraints and measurement suggestions for the playbook:
>
> 1) Failover timing: measure both (a) control-plane detection-to-route-change and (b) client-observed latency tail. Expectation: route-change within 8–12s for cross-region with KV rehydration in ~500–800ms for warmed prefixes. We'll instrument both timestamps.
>
> 2) KV cache impact: cold-cache vs warm-cache will materially affect QoE on failover. I've attached a small workbook with test vectors and expected KV hit-rate thresholds (kv-cache-impact.xlsx).
>
> 3) Rate-limiting nuance: Redwood provides per-key burst windows. For your burst tests, use a spread of keys to emulate tenant multiplexing vs single-key bursting — we'll show difference in throttle behavior.
>
> 4) Error-budget triggers: we'll surface console alerts and run the automatic fallback policy on a mirrored traffic stream (no customer-facing impact). We'll capture both the fallback decision trace and the subsequent latency/availability metrics.
>
> Marcus — can you confirm the test harness we'll use and whether we need temporary quota increases for Medisys during the run?
